answer: Each epoch sells a fixed set of voting slots in a sealed uniform-price auction, one per identity. A sybil farm bids for k seats at once and so against itself: each extra alias lifts the clearing price paid on every seat. Cost is superlinear in votes; the spend is burned, not a deposit. Weight cannot be forged by copying a key: it is a scarce seat on a quartz clock no bidder can predict. Post-auction correlation clusters aliases under one controller and forfeits them together: like shale, thin fake layers split on one plane and count as one claim. An honest agent buys one seat.
